title: Design a Supply Chain Inventory & Demand Forecasting System

spark.summary: Design an end-to-end Supply Chain Inventory & Demand Forecasting platform generating daily P10/P50/P90 forecasts for 50M SKU-Store combinations, reconciling hierarchies via MinT, and emitting MILP-optimized Purchase Orders.
spark.keyTakeaway: When durability and read throughput pull in opposite directions, unify POS sales, ERP stock, supplier lead times, and weather/promo signals in an Iceberg Feature Lakehouse feeding distributed Spark/Ray TFT training and a global MILP optimizer.
spark.byteSummary:
A global retailer with 100,000 SKUs across 500 stores (50M SKU-Store time series) needs daily demand forecasts and automated replenishment orders before morning warehouse picking begins.

POS sales, ERP inventory snapshots, supplier lead times, and promo/weather signals flow through Kafka into an Apache Iceberg Feature Lakehouse. Distributed Spark/Ray workers train Temporal Fusion Transformers (TFT) emitting P10/P50/P90 quantiles.

A MinT Hierarchy Reconciler enforces coherence across SKU-Store, Regional DC, and National tiers, feeding a Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) Inventory Optimizer that outputs Automated Purchase Orders and Stockout Alerts.

learningJourney.title: 50M Series Scale & Daily Batch Window
learningJourney.purpose: Size compute, storage, and SLA windows for 50M SKU-Store time series.

explanation.foundation: Think of **50M Series Scale & Daily Batch Window** as the intuition layer for Design a Supply Chain Inventory & Demand Forecasting System: Size compute, storage, and SLA windows for 50M SKU-Store time series.
explanation.core: 50M SKU-Store combinations x 730 days of history = 36.5B daily feature rows (~4 TB Zstd Parquet in Iceberg). The nightly forecast + MILP optimization must complete within a 4-hour batch window (00:00–04:00 UTC) so ERP Purchase Orders are ready before 05:00 warehouse shifts.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, 50m series scale & daily batch window becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Enterprise supply-chain blueprint with Flink intraday burn-rate stockout alerts, Tobit uncensoring, quantile monotonicity guards, and FVA override auditing.

decisionFramework.problem: How to implement Design a Supply Chain Inventory & Demand Forecasting System without hitting unbounded tail latency, state divergence, or operational fragility.
decisionFramework.naiveSolution: Use a single unpartitioned path with unbounded retries and synchronous global coordination.
decisionFramework.whyItFails: Global coordination serializes throughput under load, while unbounded retries amplify transient stalls into full outages.
decisionFramework.alternatives: Compare synchronous strict-consistency paths against bounded asynchronous replication, local caching, or partitioned ownership.
decisionFramework.decision: When durability and read throughput pull in opposite directions, unify POS sales, ERP stock, supplier lead times, and weather/promo signals in an Iceberg Feature Lakehouse feeding distributed Spark/Ray TFT training and a global MILP optimizer.
decisionFramework.tradeOffs: Gains predictable p99 latency and fault isolation in exchange for explicit bounding, observability, and slightly higher implementation complexity.

decisionExercise.prompt: When Design a Supply Chain Inventory & Demand Forecasting System experiences a sudden 5x traffic spike alongside a slow downstream dependency, which engineering choice best protects system stability?

options.label: Increase retry counts and remove client timeouts so every request eventually succeeds.
options.explanation: Unbounded retries multiply load on an already struggling dependency and exhaust worker pools.

options.label: Enforce strict latency budgets, bounded jittered retries, and graceful fallback or load shedding.
options.explanation: Bounding retries and isolating slow paths preserves healthy capacity and keeps tail latency predictable.

learningJourney.title: Parallel Category-Scoped MinT Reconciliation
learningJourney.purpose: Reconcile 50M forecasts without inverting a 50M x 50M matrix.

explanation.foundation: Think of **Parallel Category-Scoped MinT Reconciliation** as the intuition layer for Design a Supply Chain Inventory & Demand Forecasting System: Reconcile 50M forecasts without inverting a 50M x 50M matrix.
explanation.core: A single global MinT matrix over 50M nodes is intractable. Because product categories (e.g., Dairy, Electronics) have disjoint replenishment hierarchies, we partition reconciliation by Category x Country, reducing each MinT solve to ~50K nodes that finish in seconds per Spark executor.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, parallel category-scoped mint reconciliation becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Enterprise supply-chain blueprint with Flink intraday burn-rate stockout alerts, Tobit uncensoring, quantile monotonicity guards, and FVA override auditing.

learningJourney.title: Decomposed MILP Purchase Order Optimization
learningJourney.purpose: Generate constrained Purchase Orders and Transfer Orders within 30 minutes.

explanation.foundation: Think of **Decomposed MILP Purchase Order Optimization** as the intuition layer for Design a Supply Chain Inventory & Demand Forecasting System: Generate constrained Purchase Orders and Transfer Orders within 30 minutes.
explanation.core: Solving one MILP with 50M integer variables would time out. We decompose by Regional DC + Supplier Vendor group, optimizing multi-SKU truckloads, MOQ rounding, and DC cubic capacity in parallel across Spark workers using HiGHS.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, decomposed milp purchase order optimization becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Enterprise supply-chain blueprint with Flink intraday burn-rate stockout alerts, Tobit uncensoring, quantile monotonicity guards, and FVA override auditing.

learningJourney.title: Forecast Value Added (FVA) & Human Override Tracking
learningJourney.purpose: Measure whether planner manual overrides actually improve or hurt forecast accuracy.

explanation.foundation: Think of **Forecast Value Added (FVA) & Human Override Tracking** as the intuition layer for Design a Supply Chain Inventory & Demand Forecasting System: Measure whether planner manual overrides actually improve or hurt forecast accuracy.
explanation.core: Supply chain planners often manually override ML forecasts. Logging both the raw TFT/MinT output and the final overridden number in Iceberg enables Forecast Value Added (FVA) tracking—automatically flagging planners or SKUs where overrides consistently worsen WAPE/Bias.

knowledgeChecks.question: How do you make MinT hierarchical reconciliation and MILP optimization tractable for 50M SKU-Store series within a 4-hour nightly window?

options.text: Partition MinT by disjoint product categories using diagonal WLS, and decompose MILP by Regional DC x Vendor
options.feedback: Correct! Exploiting disjoint categories and vendor groups turns one impossible 50M-variable solve into thousands of fast parallel subproblems.

options.text: Invert a single 50M x 50M dense covariance matrix on one Spark driver
options.feedback: A 50M x 50M dense matrix would require exabytes of RAM.

options.text: Drop 95% of SKUs from the forecast
options.feedback: Dropping SKUs causes stockouts across the long tail.
Kafka is a message bus, not a mathematical optimization solver.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Domain decomposition by category and DC-vendor groups enables linear horizontal scaling.

knowledgeChecks.question: Why should automated Purchase Orders emitted by the MILP optimizer carry an idempotent key like (plan_date, dc_id, vendor_id)?

options.text: To compress Parquet files in Apache Iceberg
options.feedback: PO keys apply to ERP order submission, not Parquet compression.

options.text: So that network retries or Spark task re-executions never submit duplicate Purchase Orders to suppliers
options.feedback: Correct! Idempotent PO keys guarantee a supplier is never accidentally double-ordered on retry.

options.text: To bypass Temporal Fusion Transformer quantile checks
options.feedback: Quantile monotonicity is checked right after inference.

options.text: To disable Flink intraday stockout alerts
options.feedback: Flink alerts run independently on live POS streams.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Idempotent ERP keys prevent costly duplicate supplier orders during batch retries.

knowledgeChecks.question: What is the purpose of Forecast Value Added (FVA) tracking in an enterprise forecasting platform?

options.text: To measure whether manual planner overrides improve or worsen accuracy compared to the raw ML+MinT baseline
options.feedback: Correct! FVA audits override accuracy and captures reason codes to uncover missing model features.

options.text: To replace Apache Kafka with batch FTP
options.feedback: FVA is an accuracy governance metric, not a transport protocol.

options.text: To eliminate safety stock at Regional DCs
options.feedback: Safety stock is still required for demand and lead-time uncertainty.

options.text: To force all SKUs to use the P10 quantile

knowledgeChecks.explanation: FVA keeps human-in-the-loop overrides accountable and turns domain insights into new features.
